> DEVELOPER

As this is running, try to think about how to improve the actual process. Like what are things that are frictional or difficult to do that we could improve?

> AGENT

Current process friction worth fixing structurally: the run controller mixes “training”, “sampling”, “artifact upload”, and “human review” into one path, but each has different failure costs. The durable shape is to split it into phases: train with sampling disabled, verify final checkpoint, push checkpoints to HF, then run a separate eval/sampling phase from the HF checkpoint and only then teardown.

The second structural issue is RunPod exec itself: remote helper paths are shared across calls, so side probes can interfere with long-running jobs. That belongs in `external.runpod.exec` as per-exec remote temp dirs or a remote lock, not as operator lore.

> AGENT

A third improvement is artifact policy. Right now the old resume path assumes “copy checkpoint locally, then register,” which is the wrong default for multi-GB LoRA runs. The run should treat HF as the checkpoint store, write the HF repo/revision into `last_run.json`, and only pull review media locally.

> AGENT

Right. The eval prompts should be held-out, not lifted from dataset captions. The better target is: same grammar/tokens/camera vocabulary as training, but novel scene actions and novel dialogue, so we test generalization rather than memorization. I’ll rewrite them that way before sampling.

> AGENT

I also removed dataset loading from the eval configs entirely. Sampling doesn’t need a dataloader, and avoiding it prevents the eval run from depending on copied training clips or accidentally biasing toward training examples.

> AGENT

On alignment: partially, but not fully.

What matches the recipe you pasted:
- Base is `Lightricks/LTX-2.3/ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors`.
- LoRA rank is 32 with alpha 32.
- Optimizer is `adamw8bit`, UNet/transformer training only, text encoder off.
- Checkpoints every 250 steps.

What does **not** match:
- Our LR is `2e-5`, not `1e-4`. That is 5x lower, so learning is intentionally slower/subtler.
- Our successful run used `2000` steps across `131` clips, about `15.3 steps/clip`, not `200-250 steps/clip`.
- Sample generation during training was disabled because AI Toolkit’s in-train sampler was crashing the run; we’re doing the checkpoint sampling as a separate eval phase now.
- Our training clips are 97 frames at 24fps, just over 4s, while the held-out checkpoint eval samples are 145 frames, about 6s.

So if that Ostris tutorial guidance is the target, our run is probably **undertrained by that heuristic**, especially because the dataset is much larger than 15 clips. The current checkpoint samples being similar at 250 vs 750 is consistent with that: the files are not identical by hash, and the logs are loading separate checkpoints, but with fixed seeds/prompt and a low LR, the visual change can be subtle.

Current eval is still running on `step_1500`; `step_1250` and earlier are local. I’m continuing to watch and will pull `1500`, `1750`, and `final` as soon as each appears.

> DEVELOPER

Let's kill this and kick off another training run aligned with this except only train on the clips from the apartment, not the cafe too: Dataset

  - 19 clips, ~2–8.5s each, target ~5s, cut on sentence boundaries (Kdenlive)
  - Source: 1440p webcam, 16:9
  - Manual captions only. Format: ostress says, "<verbatim words>". Lowercase trigger, prefer a
  real-name-style trigger over a synthetic token
  - Caption speech verbatim — keep "gonna", stutters, fillers (so you can prompt them out later)
  - Describe only deviations (gestures, mid-sentence cuts). Anything you omit from the caption gets
  burned into the character — so don't describe clothes/scene if you want them locked

  Base model
  
  - LTX 2.3 base (not turbo). Train on base, infer on distilled/turbo

  Training config
  
  - Quantization: float8
  - LoRA Linear, rank 32
  - Timestep schedule: start on "high noise", switch to "balanced" near the end — never finish on
  low-noise
  - Cache text embeddings: ON (drops the text encoder)
  - Cache latents: ON (otherwise +9s/step on video)
  - Auto frame count: ON (24 fps, frames = sec*24 + 1)
  - Resolution buckets: 512 + 768 first, add 1024 on second/overnight run
  - Stopped at 5,000 steps (started planning for 30k, sampled every 2k; 3k already looked good)
  - LR / optimizer / batch size: left at AI Toolkit defaults

  Hardware

  - Demo: RTX 6000 Pro, 96 GB, used ~55 GB VRAM, ~7.7–8.2 s/it
  - Home alt: 5090 with full layer offloading, stick to 512 / short clips
  - "Low VRAM" toggle ON always for video models

  Sampling during training

  - 1024×576 for 768-bucket, 680×384 for 512-bucket — maintain 768 long-edge
  - 121 frames (5s)
  - Mix in-distribution + OOD prompts (cat, dancing, music) to probe generalization

  Inference

  - ComfyUI on LTX-2.3 distilled (turbo), even though trained on base
  - 24 fps, frames = sec*24+1
  - 10s 1080p on a 5090 in <4 min
  - Fine-detail levers: different samplers, higher CFG

  Key gotchas
  
  - Burn-in vs. describe is the central caption rule
  - High-noise-first → balanced; never end on low-noise
  - Always cache latents for video LoRAs
  - Don't blow up sample resolution during training

  Full transcript saved at /tmp/ostris-ltx/transcript.txt and ostris.en.srt if you want to dig
  further.

For the timestep schedule, the transcript confirms the intent: high-noise early to learn the broad scene/identity, then balanced at the end for detail, and avoid low-noise as the finishing phase. s['height']=384\n    s['num_frames']=121; s['fps']=24\n    s['sample_steps']=30; s['guidance_scale']=3.0\n    s['seed']=42; s['walk_seed']=True\n    s['prompts']=[\n        'seinfeld apartment, Jerry and Elaine argue at the kitchen counter in jerrys_apt. Jerry says, \"That is not a rule, that is a lifestyle.\" Elaine says, \"It is a very stupid lifestyle.\" 90s multi-cam sitcom lighting.',\n        'seinfeld apartment, George sits on the couch explaining a petty social problem while Jerry stands near the fridge. \"prompts.json\").write_text(json.dumps(prompts, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\n+\n+\n+def generate_samples() -> dict:\n+    patch_sampling_only_exit()\n+    prompts = json.loads(PROMPTS_PATH.read_text())\n+    variants = [\n+        (\"512_bucket_5s\", 680, 384, 121),\n+        (\"768_bucket_5s\", 1024, 576, 121),\n+    ]\n+    manifest = {\"repo_id\": REPO_ID, \"final_lora\": str(FINAL_LORA), \"variants\": [], \"prompts\": prompts}\n+    for kind, width, height, frames in variants:\n+        cfg = write_sample_config(kind, prompts, width, height, frames)\n+        log_path = SAMPLES_ROOT / f\"{kind}.log\"\n+        with log_path.open(\"w\") as log:\n+            proc = subprocess.run(\n+                [\"python3\", \"run.py\", str(cfg)],\n+                cwd=\"/app/ai-toolkit\",\n+                stdout=log,\n+                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,\n+                text=True,\n+            )\n+        if proc.returncode != 0:\n+            print(log_path.read_text()[-12000:])\n+            raise SystemExit(proc.returncode)\n+        normalize_outputs(kind, prompts)\n+        manifest[\"variants\"].append({\n+            \"kind\": kind,\n+            \"width\": width,\n+            \"height\": height,\n+            \"frames\": frames,\n+            \"fps\": 24,\n+            \"seconds\": frames / 24,\n+        })\n+        Path(\"/workspace/apartment_final_samples_manifest.json\").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\n+    return manifest\n+\n+\n+def main() -> None:\n+    os.environ.setdefault(\"HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER\", \"1\")\n+    upload_manifest = upload_checkpoints()\n+    sample_manifest = generate_samples()\n+    Path(\"/workspace/apartment_final_run_manifest.json\").write_text(\n+        json.dumps({\"upload\": upload_manifest, \"samples\": sample_manifest}, indent=2) + \"\\n\"\n+    )\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    main()\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

Pod is terminated: `xr7svwy94ui721` is killed, so GPU spend is stopped.

I agree this looks like “training not taking effect,” not just bad prompts. The strongest signal is what you said: early and final samples look basically the same. That points to one of these likely causes:

1. **LoRA not actually affecting inference**
   The log says the LoRA loaded with `Missing keys: []`, but that only proves the file loaded into AI Toolkit’s sampling process. We should verify whether LTX 2.3 sampling is actually applying the LoRA weights to generation. A base-vs-LoRA A/B with the same seed and a very in-distribution prompt is the fastest check.

2. **Caption/trigger mismatch**
   Training captions use `jerrys_apt`, `Scene: ...`, character names, etc. They do **not** contain the literal trigger phrase `seinfeld apartment`. AI Toolkit should inject `trigger_word`, but given the result, this is worth proving by dumping the exact final text embeddings/captions used during training.

3. **JSON caption handling**
   The dataset files are `.caption.json` with a `caption` field. If AI Toolkit is not extracting the `caption` field as intended, it may be training on weird JSON text or empty/unhelpful captions. That would explain weak or unrelated learning.

4. **Sampling on base instead of intended inference path**
   We trained on LTX 2.3 base, but sampled through AI Toolkit’s trainer sampling path, not the intended ComfyUI/turbo inference path. If that sampler path is flaky for LTX 2.3 LoRAs, the samples may be misleading.

5. **Dataset too heterogeneous for the target**
   94 clips across multiple characters, outfits, framings, and apartment angles may dilute the concept compared with Ostris’s smaller tighter character-LoRA recipe. But this alone would not explain “first and last look the same”; I’d check pipeline application first.

I would investigate in this order: verify exact captions after trigger injection, run base-vs-LoRA same-seed inference, inspect whether AI Toolkit’s LTX sampler actually applies the LoRA, then only consider retraining/data changes.

> AGENT

GPU is killed. SSH now refuses connection and RunPod teardown reports `xr7svwy94ui721` already gone, so spend should be stopped.

Most likely causes worth investigating before any retrain:

1. **Sampling may not reflect LoRA effect**
   The sample log said the LoRA loaded with `Missing keys: []`, but early and final outputs looking the same strongly suggests either the LoRA is not materially affecting inference, or the sample path is applying it at near-zero practical effect. First check should be same seed, same prompt, base vs LoRA, with a deliberately in-distribution prompt.

2. **Caption/trigger mismatch**
   The training captions are all like `Scene: ... inside jerrys_apt...`; none include the literal sample trigger `seinfeld apartment`. AI Toolkit appears to inject `trigger_word`, but we should prove the exact text passed into cached text embeddings. If it trained on `jerrys_apt` and we sampled on `Jerry's apartment / seinfeld apartment`, that could weaken the association.

3. **JSON caption extraction**
   The local AI Toolkit code does appear to handle JSON captions with a top-level `caption` field, but this is still worth a direct runtime dump from the dataloader. If `caption_ext: caption.json` is interpreted differently than expected, it could train on empty captions or raw JSON-ish text.

4. **Training target too broad**
   This run was not a narrow character LoRA; it was scene + multiple characters + many framings. That makes it harder. But it doesn’t fully explain “step 500 and final look the same,” so I’d treat this as secondary until LoRA application/captions are verified.

5. **Config mismatch with Ostris recipe**
   We used the proxy recipe, but with 94 clips and scene/multi-character objective. If the training technically worked but was too weak, next run should probably be smaller/tighter: only strongest apartment clips, exact trigger in every caption, simpler captions, and an early A/B sample at 250/500 before committing.

The concrete next debug should be: dump 3 actual training captions after AI Toolkit trigger injection/cache path, then run one base-vs-LoRA sample using exact caption-style wording: `seinfeld apartment, Scene: A wide shot inside jerrys_apt...`.

The short version: we can use existing VibeComfy workflows, and that is what the harness is doing now. I’m patching that compatibility layer rather than hand-building a separate raw workflow.

We can convert/use existing VibeComfy workflows. The issue was not “impossible”; it was that the existing LTX ready workflows are stale against current Comfy node schemas. They compile as VibeComfy workflows, but runtime nodes now require named inputs that the templates still leave as positional `widget_*` fields.

I used the existing VibeComfy LTX workflow and patched the compatibility gaps in:
[runs/seinfeld-lora-apartment-ostris-proxy-run14/vibecomfy_ab/run_vibecomfy_cloud_ab.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/Astrid/runs/seinfeld-lora-apartment-ostris-proxy-run14/vibecomfy_ab/run_vibecomfy_cloud_ab.py)

- `base_no_keyword`
- `base_with_keyword`

- `lora_with_keyword`

[runs/.../vibecomfy_ab/outputs](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/Astrid/runs/seinfeld-lora-apartment-ostris-proxy-run14/vibecomfy_ab/outputs)

I also made and opened the collage:
[runs/.../outputs/vibecomfy_ab_collage.jpg](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/Astrid/runs/seinfeld-lora-apartment-ostris-proxy-run14/vibecomfy_ab/outputs/vibecomfy_ab_collage.jpg)

The useful read: the LoRA is definitely being applied, and it visibly shifts the samples toward the apartment/Seinfeld distribution. The remaining structural fixes worth making in VibeComfy are to update the LTX ready-template widget schema, declare RES4LYF where needed, and make frame/FPS controls explicit so we don’t accidentally get one-frame smoke-test outputs.

> DEVELOPER

Do yuo think that trigger is enough, would something more unique - e.g. snfldapt - be more unique and work better?

> AGENT

A more unique trigger like `snfldapt` would probably be better for controllability, but it is not a free change mid-run because the current captions/config trained the phrase `seinfeld apartment`. The phrase is semantically useful but leaky: base LTX already has priors for “Seinfeld” and “apartment,” so it can satisfy the prompt without relying heavily on the LoRA. A synthetic trigger makes LoRA activation easier to isolate in evals, especially for LoRA-vs-base comparisons.

For this run, I would not restart just to change the trigger. I’d test both prompt forms after completion: the trained phrase `seinfeld apartment`, plus `snfldapt` only if we add it as an inference alias is unlikely to work because it was not trained. For the next training run, I’d include both in captions, e.g. `snfldapt, seinfeld apartment, ...`, so we get a unique activation token while preserving the semantic anchor.

> DEVELOPER

any benefit to adding that to the training at this stage?

> AGENT

Not much, and I would not mutate this run for it. Adding `snfldapt` now would only affect the remaining ~57% of steps, while the first 43% learned without it. That creates a mixed trigger association: `seinfeld apartment` has the full run, `snfldapt` has only late-stage exposure, and evals become harder to interpret.

If we wanted the unique token, the clean structural fix is a new run or continuation where every caption has the same prefix from step 0 of that run: `snfldapt, seinfeld apartment, ...`. For this run, the cleaner move is to finish it, evaluate with `seinfeld apartment` vs no trigger, and use the result to decide whether the next dataset/caption pass should add the synthetic token.

tool_use apply_patch
```json
{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: runs/seinfeld-lora-apartment-ostris-proxy-run15-15k/remote_scripts/compare_5k_intervals.py\n@@\n-cases = [\n-    (\"lora_with_keyword\", True, True),\n-    (\"lora_no_keyword\", True, False),\n-    (\"base_with_keyword\", False, True),\n-    (\"base_no_keyword\", False, False),\n-]\n+all_cases = [\n+    (\"lora_with_keyword\", True, True),\n+    (\"lora_no_keyword\", True, False),\n+    (\"base_with_keyword\", False, True),\n+    (\"base_no_keyword\", False, False),\n+]\n+lora_cases = [\n+    (\"lora_with_keyword\", True, True),\n+    (\"lora_no_keyword\", True, False),\n+]\n for step in (15000, 10000, 5000):\n     lora = lora_for_effective_step(step)\n+    cases = all_cases if step == 15000 else lora_cases\n     for case, use_lora, with_keyword in cases:\n         name = f\"compare_{step}_{case}\"\n+        expected = [\n+            Path(\"/workspace/final_samples_15k/flat\") / f\"{step}_{case}_{p['id']}.mp4\"\n+            for p in prompts\n+        ]\n+        if all(path.exists() for path in expected):\n+            manifest[\"comparisons\"].append({\"effective_step\": step, \"case\": case, \"use_lora\": use_lora, \"with_keyword\": with_keyword, \"checkpoint\": str(lora), \"network_multiplier\": 1.0 if use_lora else 0.0, \"files\": [str(path) for path in expected], \"skipped_existing\": True})\n+            Path(\"/workspace/final_samples_15k/manifest.json\").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + \"\\n\")\n+            continue\n         shutil.rmtree(Path(\"/workspace/final_samples_15k\") / name, ignore_errors=True)\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```

> AGENT

Yes, there is a real likely cause for the audio: we did not train audio.

The training config has no `do_audio: true`, and AI Toolkit defaults that to `false`. So the LoRA learned from video frames/captions, but not from the clips’ audio latents. The sampler is still outputting AAC audio in the MP4s, but that audio is basically base-model/generated audio from the prompt, not something the LoRA learned from the sitcom clips. Warped/broken sound is therefore not surprising.

For the visual weirdness, the key split is the base controls now running:

- If `base_with_keyword` and `base_no_keyword` look similarly broken, this is probably inference/sampling/model-path quality rather than the LoRA.
- If base looks cleaner and only LoRA looks distorted, then 15k may be overtrained or unstable, and the 10k/5k comparisons matter.
- If all AI Toolkit samples look bad but the fal run looked more normal, then we should trust fal/Comfy-style inference more than AI Toolkit’s sampler for judging this LoRA.

I’m going to keep the comparison running. For local review, I can also make muted copies/collages so the bad audio does not contaminate visual judgment.

> DEVELOPER

Would this explain why that training was low quality?

> AGENT

Partly, but not completely.

The missing `do_audio: true` explains the broken/warped audio in AI Toolkit samples. It does not by itself explain bad visuals, because the LoRA was still training on video/image latents.

For visual low quality, the more likely causes are:

- AI Toolkit sampler may be a poor judge here. The fal 10k/15k outputs are the cleaner comparison path because they use the intended inference stack and no generated audio.
- 15k may be overtrained. If 10k looked better than 15k in fal, that points to degradation from too many steps.
- The trigger/caption setup may be too weak or too broad for a multi-character scene LoRA. `seinfeld apartment` is descriptive but not unique; it may not bind strongly.
- We trained rich multi-character scene behavior from only 94 apartment clips. That is harder than Ostris’s single-character identity LoRA, so the same recipe is only a proxy.
- Our training captions and eval prompts may still be slightly mismatched, though the patched prompts improve that going forward.

So: missing audio is a real bug, but for visual quality I’d treat overtraining, inference-path mismatch, and weak/multi-concept conditioning as the main suspects.

> DEVELOPER

yeah 10k always looked crap i felt like the whole thing was degrading it as it went

> AGENT

That points away from “15k overtrained” as the main explanation. If 5k, 10k, and 15k all look worse or unrelated, the likely issue is earlier in the training setup/data contract.

Most plausible causes:

- The LoRA is learning the wrong target distribution: multi-character + set + dialogue + camera style is much broader than a character LoRA. It may smear identity/scene instead of forming a usable control.
- Caption trigger is too generic: `seinfeld apartment` may not become a strong learned handle. A unique token like `snfldapt` would probably help future runs, especially prepended consistently to every caption and prompt.
- Audio omission does not explain visual degradation, but it means the model had captions with Speech/Sounds sections while only visual latents were trained. That mismatch could still make conditioning noisier.
- The AI Toolkit LTX training config may not be hitting the exact intended LTX 2.3 recipe. We fixed obvious issues now, but the prior run had no audio and weaker eval prompts.
- Dataset may be too visually inconsistent for one LoRA target: multiple characters, poses, cuts, and possibly caption detail describing too many controllable variables can dilute the learning signal.

I would not continue from that checkpoint. I’d restart smaller and cleaner: unique trigger, audio enabled, maybe 1k/2k/3k/5k saves, and either train only apartment scene style or one/two characters first rather than the full ensemble behavior in one LoRA.

> DEVELOPER

And what rank were we training on? Could it be that, you know, we're training on too high a rank for what was possible?

> AGENT

We trained rank 32, alpha 32.

Could rank be part of it? Yes, but I would not put it first. Rank 32 is normal for Ostris-style LTX 2.3 character LoRAs, but our target is harder and noisier: multiple characters + apartment scene + sitcom style + dialogue behavior. Higher rank gives the LoRA more capacity to memorize messy correlations. With only 94 clips, that can turn into visual mush or unstable style transfer instead of a clean trigger.

For the next run, I’d try:

- Rank 16, alpha 16 as the conservative default.
- Unique trigger, e.g. `snfldapt`, in every caption and prompt.
- Audio enabled.
- Shorter checkpoint ladder: 500, 1k, 2k, 3k, maybe 5k.
- Do not continue from the current LoRA.

If rank 16 underfits but is stable, then rank 32 becomes worth revisiting with a cleaner/smaller target.

> DEVELOPER

But with a lower rank that means it doesn't have enough space for all of it because it's like a broad thing we're trying to teach it I guess.

> AGENT

Right, that’s the tradeoff. Lower rank gives it less capacity. For a broad concept, too low a rank can underfit.

But the failure mode we saw looked less like “not enough capacity” and more like “capacity used badly”: the LoRA was changing the model, but not in a coherent direction. In that case, more rank can amplify bad correlations rather than solve them.

For this target, I’d think of rank as a stabilizer, not just storage:

- Rank 16: safer test to see whether the dataset has a learnable signal at all.
- Rank 32: reasonable if captions/triggers/audio are fixed and early samples look coherent.
- Rank 64: only if rank 32 clearly underfits but stays stable.

Because we’re teaching a broad ensemble scene, I’d actually keep rank 32 if we split the concept better: unique trigger, audio enabled, cleaner captions, shorter early checkpoints. If we want a diagnostic run, rank 16 is useful because if even rank 16 immediately degrades the base, the issue is probably not “rank too low”; it’s data/config/objective.

```json
{
```
```json
  "cmd": "PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 - <<'PY'\nimport json, subprocess, re, html\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom faster_whisper import WhisperModel\n\nRUN=Path('runs/frank-reynolds-lora-run1')\nSRC=RUN/'sources'\nTRANS=RUN/'transcripts'\nCAND=RUN/'candidate_clips'\nTRANS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nCAND.mkdir(exist_ok=True)\nmodel=WhisperModel('base', device='cpu', compute_type='int8')\nall_items=[]\nfor src in sorted(SRC.glob('*.mp4')):\n    jpath=TRANS/(src.stem+'.json')\n    if jpath.exists():\n        data=json.loads(jpath.read_text())\n    else:\n        print('transcribe', src.name, flush=True)\n        segments, info=model.transcribe(str(src), beam_size=5, word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=True)\n        data={'source':str(src),'duration':info.duration,'segments':[]}\n        for s in segments:\n            text=' '.join(s.text.strip().split())\n            if text:\n                data['segments'].append({'start':float(s.start),'end':float(s.end),'text':text})\n        jpath.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2)+\"\\n\")\n    segs=data['segments']\n    i=0\n    while i < len(segs):\n        text=segs[i]['text']\n        start=segs[i]['start']\n        end=segs[i]['end']\n        # merge short adjacent transcript chunks up to a usable 2-8.5s window.\n        j=i+1\n        while (end-start) < 3.0 and j < len(segs) and (segs[j]['end']-start) <= 8.5:\n            text += ' ' + segs[j]['text']\n            end = segs[j]['end']\n            j += 1\n        # also allow one contiguous follow-up if still under cap and the current text is fragmentary.\n        if j < len(segs) and (end-start) < 6.0 and (segs[j]['end']-start) <= 8.5 and len(text.split()) < 11:\n            text += ' ' + segs[j]['text']\n            end = segs[j]['end']\n            j += 1\n        dur=end-start\n        words=len(text.split())\n        lower=text.lower()\n        # Toss obvious non-Frank/interviewer filler and ultra-short reactions.\n        bad=(words < 4 or lower in {'okay.','wow.','thank you.'} or lower.startswith(('good morning','with us today')) or 'mr. reynolds' in lower or 'were you concerned' in lower)\n        if 2.0 <= dur <= 8.7 and not bad:\n            all_items.append({'source':str(src),'source_stem':src.stem,'start':max(0,start-0.08),'end':min(data['duration'],end+0.08),'text':text})\n        i=max(j, i+1)\n\n# Prefer clips with Frank-ish first-person/known phrases, but retain diversity across sources.\nkeywords=['i ', \"i'm\", 'my ', 'me ', 'frank', 'blasting', 'egg', 'rum', 'warthog', 'gun', 'pilot', 'cocaine', 'frog', 'gablogian', 'crab', 'beer']\ndef score(item):\n    t=item['text'].lower()\n    return sum(1 for k in keywords if k in t) + min(len(t.split()), 18)/18\nby_source={}\nfor item in sorted(all_items, key=score, reverse=True):\n    by_source.setdefault(item['source_stem'], [])\n    if len(by_source[item['source_stem']]) < 2:\n        by_source[item['source_stem']].append(item)\nselected=[]\nfor stem in sorted(by_source):\n    selected.extend(by_source[stem])\nselected=sorted(selected, key=lambda x: (x['source_stem'], x['start']))[:36]\n\nmanifest={'clips':[],'trigger':'frnkphl','caption_style':'single-character Frank Reynolds LoRA'}\nfor idx,item in enumerate(selected,1):\n    out=CAND/f'frnkphl_{idx:03d}.mp4'\n    dur=item['end']-item['start']\n    if not out.exists():\n        subprocess.run([\n            'ffmpeg','-y','-hide_banner','-loglevel','error',\n            '-ss',f\"{item['start']:.3f}\",'-i',item['source'],'-t',f\"{dur:.3f}\",\n            '-vf','scale=trunc(min(768,iw)/2)*2:-2,fps=24',\n            '-c:v','libx264','-preset','veryfast','-crf','18','-c:a','aac','-ar','48000','-ac','2',str(out)\n        ], check=True)\n    q=item['text'].replace('\"','\\\\\"')\n    caption={\n        'caption': f'frnkphl says, \"{q}\". Frank Reynolds, an older short bald man, speaks in a chaotic Philadelphia bar-sitcom scene.',\n        'trigger': 'frnkphl',\n        'character': 'Frank Reynolds',\n        'spoken_words': item['text'],\n        'source': item['source'],\n        'source_start': item['start'],\n        'source_end': item['end'],\n    }\n    cap=out.with_suffix('.caption.json')\n    cap.write_text(json.dumps(caption, indent=2)+\"\\n\")\n    manifest['clips'].append({'clip_id':out.stem,'clip_file':str(out),'caption_file':str(cap),'duration':dur,'text':item['text'],'source':item['source'],'source_start':item['start'],'source_end':item['end']})\n(RUN/'candidate_manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2)+\"\\n\")\nprint('candidate clips', len(manifest['clips']))\nfor c in manifest['clips'][:40]:\n    print(c['clip_id'], f\"{c['duration']:.2f}s\", c['text'][:100])\nPY",
```

I found the real problem with the current run before letting it burn money: it made it past the old optimizer failure, but it is running with `gradient_accumulation: 4`, so each “step” is four backward passes. That is why it is ~30s/step and would take roughly 40+ hours for 5k; I’m switching it to accumulation 1, which matches the “AI Toolkit defaults” direction much better and should bring the runtime back into the expected range while reusing the cached latents/text embeddings.

I am gonna get real weird with it.\".',\n+    },\n+    \"frnkphl_015\": {\n+        \"start\": 3.0,\n+        \"end\": None,\n+        \"caption\": 'frnkphl says, \"Well, I went in for a loaf of bread. I took some skis.\".',\n+    },\n+}\n+\n+\n+def ffprobe_duration(path: Path) -> float:\n+    result = subprocess.run(\n+        [\n+            \"ffprobe\",\n+            \"-v\",\n+            \"error\",\n+            \"-show_entries\",\n+            \"format=duration\",\n+            \"-of\",\n+            \"default=nw=1:nk=1\",\n+            str(path),\n+        ],\n+        check=True,\n+        text=True,\n+        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,\n+    )\n+    return float(result.stdout.strip())\n+\n+\n+def trim_video(src: Path, dst: Path, start: float, end: float | None) -> None:\n+    args = [\"ffmpeg\", \"-y\", \"-hide_banner\", \"-loglevel\", \"error\", \"-ss\", f\"{start:.3f}\"]\n+    if end is not None:\n+        args += [\"-t\", f\"{max(0.01, end - start):.3f}\"]\n+    args += [\"-i\", str(src), \"-c:v\", \"libx264\", \"-preset\", \"veryfast\", \"-crf\", \"18\", \"-c:a\", \"aac\", \"-b:a\", \"160k\", str(dst)]\n+    subprocess.run(args, check=True)\n+\n+\n+def copy_caption(path: Path, caption: str) -> None:\n+    path.write_text(json.dumps({\"caption\": caption}, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+\n+\n+def main() -> None:\n+    manifest = json.loads(SRC_MANIFEST.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n+    if OUT_DIR.exists():\n+        shutil.rmtree(OUT_DIR)\n+    OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True)\n+\n+    out_clips: list[dict] = []\n+    for item in manifest[\"clips\"]:\n+        clip_id = item[\"clip_id\"]\n+        if clip_id in DROP:\n+            continue\n+\n+        src_video = Path(item[\"clip_file\"])\n+        src_duration = ffprobe_duration(src_video)\n+        out_item = dict(item)\n+        out_video = OUT_DIR / f\"{clip_id}.mp4\"\n+        out_caption = OUT_DIR / f\"{clip_id}.caption.json\"\n+\n+        if clip_id in TRIMS:\n+            spec = TRIMS[clip_id]\n+            start = float(spec[\"start\"])\n+            end = spec[\"end\"]\n+            end = src_duration if end is None else float(end)\n+            trim_video(src_video, out_video, start, end)\n+            out_item[\"user_trim\"] = {\"relative_start_sec\": start, \"relative_end_sec\": end}\n+            out_item[\"source_start\"] = round(float(out_item[\"source_start\"]) + start, 3)\n+            out_item[\"source_end\"] = round(float(out_item[\"source_start\"]) + (end - start), 3)\n+            out_item[\"duration\"] = round(ffprobe_duration(out_video), 3)\n+            out_item[\"quote\"] = spec[\"caption\"].split('\"', 1)[1].rsplit('\"', 1)[0]\n+            out_item[\"caption\"] = spec[\"caption\"]\n+        else:\n+            shutil.copy2(src_video, out_video)\n+            shutil.copy2(Path(item[\"caption_file\"]), out_caption)\n+            out_item[\"duration\"] = round(ffprobe_duration(out_video), 3)\n+\n+        if clip_id in TRIMS:\n+            copy_caption(out_caption, out_item[\"caption\"])\n+\n+        out_item[\"clip_file\"] = str(out_video)\n+        out_item[\"caption_file\"] = str(out_caption)\n+        out_clips.append(out_item)\n+\n+    out_manifest = {\n+        **{k: v for k, v in manifest.items() if k != \"clips\"},\n+        \"selection_policy\": {\n+            **manifest.get(\"selection_policy\", {}),\n+            \"user_edit_pass\": \"Dropped 005/006/007/008/010; trimmed 009/011/013/014/015 per user review.\",\n+            \"needs_replacements\": 15 - len(out_clips),\n+        },\n+        \"clips\": out_clips,\n+    }\n+    OUT_MANIFEST.write_text(json.dumps(out_manifest, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + \"\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n+    print(f\"wrote {len(out_clips)} clips to {OUT_DIR}\")\n+    print(f\"manifest {OUT_MANIFEST}\")\n+\n+\n+if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n+    main()\n*** End Patch\n"
```json
}
```
